items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: I say, and you're going to always get a staccato instead of a legato, and you'll sound Willie Smith. That's what I was doing.

ctx.x: That's what I've been trying to figure out here. James Richmond was in the band, Buster Smith, and that's when Charlie started to playing. And we used to go down to the pool hall every day, James Richmond would follow, on the pool hall, and I was down there,and Charlie Christian came in, you know. And he had an old acoustic guitar. (Inaudible.) He say, how do you sound like that saxophone? I say, if you play the downstroke, Charlie, you gotta be fast or it don't never come out. And I say, and you're going to…

And I showed him, and he took the guitar. And he sat down and he did it, and in a few minutes, he had it. I say, both this guy put everbody out of business in a few months. I say, you got it, and he picked right up on it. Must had been playing a little somewhere.
